title: Q-RETENTION-1: every append-only table declares a retention, and a daily prune enforces it
body:
**Owner:** operations
**Trigger:** executor tick, driver order
**Done check:** grep:seed/worker/src/retention.js::export async function pruneAll
**Status:** closed

Lesson from the fleet this account was split from (frozen 2026-11-16): its audit database grew to 1,011 tables. 266 of them were `bak_*` copies made before deletes and never removed, and append-only ledgers kept every row forever. Storage cost little, but every view and trigger over them read more rows each tick. Ultrastable keeps the same kinds of ledgers (tick_runs, dispatches, outcomes, budget_ledger, cost_samples, criticality_samples, handoff_events, loop_beats, hits) with no stated retention.

Acceptance: a table in seed/autonomy/retention.json lists each append-only table with keep_days (or `forever` with a reason); seed/worker/src/retention.js deletes older rows once a day (gated like seed/analytics prune) and writes one row per table to a prune log; a backup table made by a migration carries an expiry and is dropped after it; test/plan-limits.test.mjs fails when a migration creates a table that retention.json does not list.

Test plan: node tests for the prune (rows past keep_days removed, newer kept, once a day) and the listing check.

size: S

**Closing probe:** grep:seed/worker/src/retention.js::export async function pruneAll

**Evidence:** seed/worker/src/retention.js pruneAll, rules in seed/autonomy/retention.json, tests seed/worker/test/retention.test.js (3) and test/plan-limits.test.mjs (every created table listed).
